explanations: luna: The section links the orphan's name with goodness that can arrive late; this covenant commands good treatment of orphans, placing timely care among obligations. | terra: Israel's covenant couples worship of God with good conduct toward orphans; care is treated as a standing communal obligation, not an accidental kindness.
terra: Each community has a direction, people are told to race toward good, and God will bring everyone together; orientation, forward movement, and gathering share one ayah.

luna: The section's horses return when called by their keeper; this verse likens disbelievers to one calling animals that hear only cries and calls, showing a voice that reaches ears without understanding.

luna: The section presents orphan care as a response to someone vulnerable; this verse counts giving wealth to orphans among righteousness, making provision an act of faith. | terra: True piety includes giving cherished wealth to orphans; it identifies the “good” that must cross the delay named by the section's orphan etymology.

luna: The section's orphan is someone whose support may be delayed; this verse directs spending of good wealth to orphans among the first named recipients. | terra: When believers ask what to spend, orphans are named among the direct recipients; the answer maps beneficence toward the one for whom it otherwise comes slowly.

luna: The section links the orphan to delayed goodness; this verse says setting their affairs right is best, الإصلاح لهم خير, and treats them as brothers. | terra: The ayah calls setting orphans' affairs right “best” and makes them members of the believers' household; it answers delayed beneficence with repair and incorporation into a protecting group.
terra: Abraham is told to call the birds and they will come swiftly; the ayah stages the section's secondary sense of calling dispersed animals so that they return to the caller's voice.
terra: Horses and livestock are listed among the attractions of the nearer life, while the best return is with God; animal wealth is bounded by the first/latter valuation developed in the section.

luna: The section names the root w-j-d for finding a lost camel; this verse repeatedly has Zakariyya find provision with Mary in her sanctuary, making finding an act of sustenance for someone under care.
terra: The martyrs rejoice over those behind them who have not yet joined them; the ayah turns the rear of a company into members still expected to catch up.

luna: The section's orphan receives shelter after being found; this verse commands guardians to hand orphans their property and forbids replacing good with bad. | terra: The command to give orphans their property and not consume it ensures that withheld good reaches the one for whom it was delayed.

luna: The section's instruction not to oppress the orphan is made concrete here by justice toward orphan girls and the fear of wronging them. | terra: Fear of injustice toward orphaned girls governs whom and how people may marry; the ayah makes the orphan's delayed or withheld due a test of justice in household formation.

luna: The section names the orphan as one to whom good can arrive late; this verse requires testing until maturity and then delivering their property when judgment is sound. | terra: Guardians test orphans until maturity and then deliver their property; this makes the section's “good that reaches the orphan late” a regulated delay ending in restitution.

luna: The section's orphan is among those needing timely provision; this verse gives orphans present at an inheritance division a share and calls for kind words. | terra: When orphans attend an estate division, they must receive provision and kind speech; the ayah prevents them from remaining at the rear of a distribution they witness.

luna: The section makes the orphan's delayed care visible; this neighboring inheritance verse tells guardians to consider the weak descendants they may leave behind, extending the orphan's vulnerability to dependents after a death.

luna: The section's image is a vulnerable orphan finally received into care; this verse reverses that care by warning that those who consume orphans' property unjustly consume fire. | terra: Those who consume orphans' wealth turn the good due to them into fire for themselves; the ayah exposes predation by the very people meant to safeguard delayed provision.

luna: The section's orphan is a named recipient of care; this verse includes orphans among those to whom believers must do good. | terra: Worship of God is joined to doing good to parents, kin, and orphans; the ayah places the fatherless within the human circle charged to bring them good.

luna: The section's orphan-care command meets a direct ruling here: when asked about women orphans, the verse commands justice toward them. | terra: The ayah addresses orphaned women to whom people do not give what is prescribed and commands justice for orphans; it exposes the human act that makes good arrive late.
terra: The Israelites are condemned to wander bewildered through the land for forty years; this is the section's directionless condition expanded from one lost animal to an entire people.

terra: God denies instituting the sāʾiba and related livestock taboos; the deliberately released animal from the section's dictionary is here bounded by a rejection of falsely attributing such release to God.

luna: The section gathers a flock into a known home under its owner; this verse calls animals communities like people and says they will be gathered to their Lord. | terra: Animals on earth and birds in flight are communities, and all are finally gathered to their Lord; the ayah combines flock, gathering, and the owner named as Rabb in the section.
terra: A person wanders bewildered on earth while companions call “come to us,” and the ayah identifies God's guidance as the true guidance; lostness, a directional call, and return meet exactly.

luna: The section's lost animal is defined by not knowing its way; this verse says stars guide people through the darknesses of land and sea, لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر. | terra: Stars are appointed so people may find their way through the darknesses of land and sea; the lost searcher is given concrete directional signs.
terra: God produces humanity from one soul and knows its settled place and repository; the vocabulary of fixed and temporary location parallels the herd's stable place and its movement away from it.

luna: The section names livestock as النعم because of their good; this verse distinguishes cattle for carrying from those for other uses and tells people to eat from God's provision. | terra: Among livestock God creates animals for burden and others close to the ground, then commands people to eat His provision; the herd contains different positions and capacities under one Provider.

terra: The ayah names the male and female of sheep and goats and asks whether either sex or what the female wombs contain was forbidden; with 6:144 it directly develops animal sex, maternity, and invented distinctions.

terra: The ayah names the male and female of camels and cattle while rejecting invented sex-based prohibitions; that boundary illuminates the dictionary statement that the designation of a lost camel applies equally to male and female.

luna: The section makes the orphan's delayed good visible; this verse protects orphan property until maturity and requires fair measure and weight. | terra: The orphan's property may be approached only in the best way until maturity; the protective waiting period makes delay serve the orphan rather than the guardian.
terra: Ṣāliḥ calls the sign “God's she-camel” and commands his people to let her graze in God's land; animal, divine ownership, and released grazing are all explicit.

luna: The section's animal is lost but can be led home; this verse compares the heedless to cattle and says they are more astray, بل هم أضل, reversing the animal's relation to guidance. | terra: People who fail to understand and perceive are compared with livestock and called still more astray; it reverses the cared-for herd into a moral picture of creatures refusing guidance.

luna: The section develops shelter and provision for a vulnerable wanderer; this verse says God sheltered an oppressed community, strengthened it, and provided good things, آواكم ورزقكم. | terra: God reminds a vulnerable, fearful group that He sheltered them, فَـَٔاوَىٰكُمْ, strengthened them, and provided good things; shelter and provision are the acts that bring the exposed back into safety.

luna: The section's orphan needs what sustains him; this verse assigns orphans a share of war gains alongside other recipients. | terra: Orphans receive a named share of spoils; communal wealth is routed to those whose good might otherwise be delayed.

luna: The section develops shelter as taking in a vulnerable orphan or stray; this verse names believers who gave shelter and support to the emigrants, آووا ونصروا, as a communal form of care. | terra: The emigrants and those who gave them shelter and support become protecting allies; the shelter-root describes incorporation of exposed people into a responsible community.

luna: The section's dictionary meaning of shelter is a creature's refuge; this verse again describes believers who sheltered and aided the emigrants, extending refuge to people in need. | terra: Those who believe, migrate, and shelter and support others are called the true believers; giving refuge is treated as the act that makes a scattered group one loyal company.

luna: The section's root ʿ-y-l names a needy person as well as one left without direction; this verse names fear of poverty, عيلة, and promises enrichment from God. | terra: The ayah places عَيْلَةً, need, beside God's promise يُغْنِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ, enriching you; it is the Quran's closest lexical expansion of the movement from عَآئِلًا to فَأَغْنَىٰ in the section.
terra: The hypocrites would bolt toward any refuge, cave, or place of entry they could find; their frantic search for shelter reverses the responsive return to a known keeper's fold.
terra: The foremost first emigrants and helpers are followed by later believers in excellence; the Quran explicitly makes a morally ordered company from leaders at the front and those following them.
terra: The people around Medina are told not to remain behind God's messenger; it turns lagging behind a leader into failure to share the leader's arduous route.
luna: The section defines مأوى as a creature's refuge and shows the lost receiving guidance; this verse says God calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.
terra: The ayah asks whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy to be followed than one needing guidance; it articulates the relation between the hādī at the front and those following.

luna: The section calls the herd's fixed place its dictionary form مرب; this verse says every creature has provision and a known settled place and deposit, مستقرها ومستودعها. | terra: Every creature's provision rests with God, who knows its dwelling and its place of deposit; this answers the image of an animal lost in an unknown waste with the Owner's complete knowledge and sustenance.
terra: Noah's son says he will take refuge on a mountain, سَـَٔاوِىٓ, but is told there is no protector that day; it marks the limit of a shelter chosen apart from the true Owner's call.
luna: The section pictures a herdsman who owns and leads the wandering animal; this verse says every moving creature is held by its forelock and names the Lord, آخذ بناصيتها.
terra: Ṣāliḥ again identifies God's she-camel and tells the people to leave her to feed in God's earth; it directly stages a female camel released to pasture while still belonging to a named owner.
terra: Lot wishes for strength or a firm support to which he could take refuge; the shelter-root names the need for a protecting place when one's household is exposed.

terra: Pharaoh leads his people on the Resurrection and brings them into the Fire, which the ayah calls an evil watering place; a leader drives his herd-like following to destructive water rather than safe pasture.

terra: Joseph's brothers accuse their father of manifest error because he loves Joseph and his brother more; within the lost-child story, ضَلَال denotes mistaken judgment rather than physical disappearance, preserving a secondary sense that matters.
terra: A brother proposes putting Joseph in the well so that a passing caravan will pick him up; it deliberately turns a known child into an apparently ownerless foundling awaiting a finder.

terra: Joseph's brothers ask that he be sent with them to roam or graze and play; this pastoral departure immediately precedes the child's separation from his father and frames him as the vulnerable member taken out with the company.
terra: Jacob fears that a wolf will eat Joseph while the brothers are heedless of him; the owner-parent anticipates exactly the loss of one entrusted member while its keepers fail to watch.

terra: The brothers return claiming that a wolf ate Joseph while they raced; their story presents the missing member as an animal-like pastoral loss, while the surrounding narrative preserves the father's knowledge that the account is false.

luna: The parallel is limited: the section's lost animal is restored to care, while a caravan discovers Joseph in a well and hides him for sale. This is a specific found-vulnerable-person scene with an exploitative outcome. | terra: A caravan draws Joseph from the well and announces that it has found a boy, then hides him as merchandise; this is a found lost child whose true family ownership remains concealed.
terra: The Egyptian who acquires the found Joseph orders that his lodging be made honorable; the lost child of 12:19 moves into shelter, though separated from the father who knows him.
terra: Joseph calls the human master who housed him “my rabb” and says that master made his lodging good; the ayah directly joins the section's owner-sense of Rabb to a protected dwelling.
terra: Joseph draws his separated brother into his own lodging, ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ, and reveals their kinship; shelter here is reunion with the one who knows who the vulnerable arrival is.
terra: Jacob turns away grieving for the still-lost Joseph until his eyes whiten; this gives the section's searching owner an affective human counterpart whose loss remains known across years.
terra: Jacob sends his sons to search carefully for Joseph and his brother and forbids despair; the lost one's kin know whom they have lost and actively seek him, as the section says of the owner.
terra: Before Joseph physically returns, Jacob recognizes his scent from afar; the lost one is known by the one who loves him even while the surrounding family doubts.
terra: When Jacob detects Joseph's scent, his family calls it his “old error”; the word for straying is applied to the very father whose recognition of the lost one is about to be vindicated.
terra: The bearer brings Joseph's shirt and Jacob's sight returns; the long search reaches a bodily sign of reunion, completing the movement begun by the scent in 12:94.
terra: Joseph receives his parents into his own protection and tells the family to enter Egypt safely; the root of shelter describes a scattered household gathered into security.
terra: Every people has a guide; the statement broadens the section's foremost hādī from an animal line into a human community's directional office.
terra: Immediately before the foremost and lagging of 15:24, God says that He gives life, causes death, and remains the inheritor; the whole moving company passes while its Owner remains.

terra: The section defines the one in front against the one left behind; this ayah names exactly ٱلْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ and ٱلْمُسْتَـْٔخِرِينَ, turning the herd's two positions into an all-encompassing divine knowledge.
terra: Immediately after God knows the foremost and lagging, the Lord gathers them all; it completes the ordered line as a company recovered into one assembly.

luna: The section says the dictionary form النعم names camels for the good and blessing in them; 16:5 presents livestock as warmth, benefit, and food. | terra: The livestock of 16:6 are first introduced as God's creation containing warmth, benefits, and food; it explains why the herd itself can bear the section's name of good and blessing.

luna: The section's camel dictionary form describes setting out to graze in the morning; 16:6 gives the flock's evening return and morning release as beauty and benefit, grounding its daily movement. | terra: This is the section's explicit Quranic herd scene: livestock are brought home in the evening and sent out in the morning, supplying both the foldward return and the day's departure to pasture.

luna: The section names the camel's front and rear saddle pieces; this neighboring livestock passage adds their loads carried to distant lands, another concrete use of the herd. | terra: After the herd's morning departure and evening return, livestock carry burdens to distant lands; this extends the ordered herd into a traveling train whose pace and rear matter.

luna: The section's dictionary examples include horses and their leading parts; this continuation names horses, mules, and donkeys as riding animals and adornment. | terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are created for riding and adornment; this supplies the Quranic setting for the section's secondary horse, rider, neck, and leading-animal details.

luna: The section's grazing scene is supplied by water and trees; this verse says the rain provides drink and trees in which people pasture their animals, فيه تسيمون. | terra: God sends water and grows vegetation “in which you pasture” livestock; this supplies the pasture toward which the section's herd sets out at the beginning of the day.

luna: The section's dictionary form هادي names a leader at the head; this verse says people are guided by the stars, وبالنجم هم يهتدون, a concrete wayfinding parallel. | terra: Landmarks and stars are means by which people are guided; the foremost guide of the section is complemented by fixed signs that orient a moving company.
terra: Every blessing people possess is from God, and in distress they cry to Him; it makes the niʿma associated with the herd traceable to the same divine Owner.
terra: Birds are made serviceable in the open sky and none holds them except God; the image gives the scattered flying creatures a keeper even away from any visible enclosure.

luna: The section defines مأوى as a place of refuge; this verse says God made homes from livestock hides and furnishings from their wool, hair, and fur, tying animal life to shelter. | terra: God makes homes places of rest and tents from livestock hides that are light during travel and encampment; the herd itself supplies a portable fold-like shelter.

luna: The section's instruction against harming orphans is expressed here as a ban on approaching their property except in the best way until maturity. | terra: The same boundary protects an orphan's property until maturity and couples it with fulfillment of covenants; delayed delivery remains an accountable trust.
terra: On the day God calls, people answer with praise and think they remained only briefly; the call brings the absent dead into responsive return.

luna: The section defines مأوى as any place a creature resorts to for shelter; these young men take refuge in a cave, أوى الفتية إلى الكهف, making refuge a chosen protection. | terra: The youths take refuge in the cave and ask their Lord for mercy and right direction; the prayer joins shelter with guidance before 18:16 describes the refuge prepared for them.

luna: The section's found animal is called back into a sheltering place; the young men tell one another to take refuge in the cave, فأووا إلى الكهف, a parallel act of gathering into safety. | terra: The youths are told to take refuge in the cave, يَأْوِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ, where their Lord will spread mercy and prepare ease; the fold-like shelter is explicitly under Rabb's care.

luna: After 18:16 tells the youths to take refuge in the cave, this verse describes the sun passing around them and says whoever God guides is guided, joining shelter to divine protection and direction. | terra: Within the cave-refuge passage, the one God guides is guided, while the one He lets stray has no protecting guide; shelter and direction are shown to depend on the same divine keeper.
luna: The section defines a refuge as a place a creature resorts to; this continuation places the cave youths' dog at the entrance, a concrete animal at the threshold of shelter.
terra: God gathers all people and leaves none behind; the final collection answers the image of a procession with a laggard or missing member by explicitly excluding any omission.

luna: The section follows an animal from loss into a search; here two travelers forget their fish and it slips into the sea, turning loss into the event that begins their search. | terra: Moses and his servant forget their fish, which takes its way into the sea; this begins a literal lost-creature episode whose route must be recovered.

luna: The section's owner seeks what went missing; the attendant recalls where the fish was lost at the rock, and 18:64 completes this row's contribution by naming it what they sought and prompting their return. | terra: The servant recalls the fish at the rock and admits forgetting it while it took a remarkable route; the lost animal is connected to failed recollection and a now-identifiable location.

luna: The section's root w-j-d links finding with the end of a search; Moses recognizes the lost fish's location as what they sought and retraces their steps, turning loss into a guide. | terra: Moses says the lost fish's place is what they were seeking, and the two retrace their own footprints; this gives the section a precise Quranic scene of search ending by following a track backward.

luna: The section says finding the lost can lead to guidance; at the marked location Moses and his attendant find a servant of God and ask to follow him, making the find a meeting with a guide. | terra: After Moses and his servant retrace the route of the lost fish, they find the servant of God they were meant to meet; recovering the missed place leads to the intended guide.

luna: The section says goodness can be slow to reach an orphan; Khidr repairs a wall hiding the two orphans' treasure so they can retrieve it when they mature, a provision deliberately kept for their future. | terra: Two orphan boys have a treasure preserved until maturity because their father was righteous; the father's absence and a good deliberately delayed until it can safely reach them concretize both dictionary claims about orphanhood.
terra: The speakers say that what is before them, behind them, and between belongs to God, then add that the Lord is never forgetful; the line's positions and the unfailing Owner appear together.
terra: The God-conscious are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation; this is a collective return to the Owner rather than an accidental massing.
terra: The guilty are driven toward Hell as a thirsty herd; the pastoral verb and thirst make this the punitive opposite of livestock led to water and shelter.
terra: Everyone in the heavens and earth comes to the Merciful as a servant; it states the ownership relation that 19:94 then renders as exact encompassing and counting.
terra: God has fully encompassed and exactly counted every creature who comes to Him; the Owner knows each member individually, so no one in the gathered company is anonymous or lost.
terra: Each creature comes to God individually on the Resurrection; even within the universal gathering, every member reaches the Owner as a known individual.
luna: The section's lost owner does not know which way to go; Moses, travelling at night, hopes to find guidance at a fire, أجد على النار هدى, a concrete search for direction.

luna: The section explicitly places Moses's staff beside a herd: 20:18 says he shakes leaves down for his sheep, making the staff part of their feeding scene. | terra: Moses identifies his staff by saying he uses it to beat down fodder for his sheep; it is the section's explicit Quranic meeting between the guiding staff and a tended flock.

terra: The infant Moses is cast into the river, taken by an enemy, and kept under God's watch and bestowed love; apparent abandonment is bounded by an Owner who never loses sight of the exposed child.
terra: Moses' sister tracks him, he is returned to his mother, rescued, tested, and brought at a measured time; this completes the lost child's recovery into maternal shelter and care.

luna: The section's dictionary form هادي means the foremost animal or leader; Moses says the Lord gave each thing its form and then guided it, linking creation with directed life. | terra: Moses says the Lord gave every created thing its form and then guided it; guidance belongs to the creator-owner and extends beyond verbal instruction to each creature's fitted way.

luna: The section describes a human owner losing track of a camel; Moses says his Lord neither strays nor forgets, لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى, making divine care unlike human loss. | terra: Moses says knowledge is with his Lord in a record and that his Lord neither loses track nor forgets, لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّى وَلَا يَنسَى; it is the decisive boundary on the image of an owner who cannot locate his animal.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of grazing meets the command to eat and pasture livestock, كلوا وارعوا أنعامكم; pasture is the animal's ordinary provision. | terra: The command to eat and pasture your livestock places human food and the herd's grazing within one provision; it makes the day's pasture a sign of the Provider.
terra: Pharaoh leads his people astray and does not guide them; he is the direct opposite of a hādī who occupies the front in order to bring those behind to the right place.
terra: On that day everyone follows the caller without deviation; the section's voice that recalls an animal becomes a universal summons whose company cannot stray from the call.
luna: The section describes a lost one receiving guidance; this verse promises that whoever follows God's guidance will neither go astray nor suffer, فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل ولا يشقى.

luna: The section's dictionary form هادي means the leading animal or guide; this verse calls Abraham's descendants leaders who guide by God's command, connecting headship with directed care. | terra: God makes the prophets leaders who guide by His command; this states directly the relation implied by the dictionary's hādī as the foremost member of a company.
terra: A people's sheep stray into a field by night and their owners' loss requires judgment; this is a concrete Quranic case of a flock crossing its proper boundary.

terra: After the straying-sheep judgment, God gives Solomon the right understanding and subjects birds to praise with David; it resolves the flock's disputed trespass and joins that scene to divinely ordered birds.

terra: Sacrificial camels stand in lines and are said to contain good for people; their ordered stance and فِيهَا خَيْرٌ meet the section's line of camels and its derivation of livestock from good and blessing.

luna: The section connects livestock with blessing; this verse spells out cattle's milk, many benefits, and food, making their favor perceptible. | terra: Livestock provide milk, many benefits, and food; the ayah makes the herd a sustained provision and supports the section's association of anʿām with good.
terra: Mary and Jesus are sheltered on a secure height with rest and flowing water; the root of مأوى here names a provisioned refuge for exposed dependents.
terra: Those who hasten in good deeds are described as foremost in them; the forward position becomes eagerness in delivering the very good that otherwise arrives late.

luna: The section says God found the needy and made him self-sufficient; this verse promises to enrich poor people from His bounty, يغنهم الله من فضله. | terra: The poor are promised that God will enrich them from His bounty; this repeats the section's movement from need to sufficiency as a divine act.
terra: Those unable to marry must remain chaste until God enriches them from His bounty; unlike 24:32's immediate promise, this ayah explicitly joins present lack to awaited sufficiency.
terra: A thirsty person follows a mirage in a level waste, finds nothing there, and instead finds God; the directionless desert search reaches the true Owner rather than the expected provision.
terra: Birds with wings outspread each know their prayer and glorification, while God knows what they do; the flying ranks remain individually known to their Lord.

luna: The section's lost animal cannot find its direction; this verse says the opponents have strayed and cannot find a way, ضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا, a moral use of the same root set against the physical image.
luna: The section's herd follows its keeper; this verse describes a person who takes his desire as god, and 25:44 completes the contrast by likening such heedlessness to cattle that are more astray.

luna: The section's flock responds to a keeper's call; this verse compares unreasoning people to cattle and calls them more astray in the way, بل هم أضل سبيلا. | terra: Those who do not hear or reason are like livestock and even further astray from the way; the herd here marks the boundary between being tended and being directionless.
terra: The prayer asks God to make the faithful leaders for the God-conscious; it seeks the front position as responsibility for those who come behind.
terra: Pharaoh's forces pursue Moses' company at sunrise; the moving group at the beginning of day sets up the apparent loss of every route and the promise of guidance in 26:62.
terra: With the pursuers behind and the sea ahead, Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him; Rabb as owner-guide answers a whole company that seems to have nowhere to go.
terra: The she-camel has an assigned drinking day and the people have theirs; the animal's place in a measured watering order extends the section's ordered herd.
terra: Solomon is taught the speech of birds and recognizes what he has been given; that communicative bond makes his later notice of one missing bird and its answering report intelligible.
terra: Solomon's hosts, including birds, are gathered and kept in ordered ranks; this is the section's moving line at the scale of a whole mixed company and sets up the missing hoopoe.

terra: As Solomon's ordered host reaches the ants, an ant calls its company into their dwellings so they will not be crushed; a voice gathers vulnerable creatures into shelter before a leading procession.
terra: After hearing the ant's sheltering call, Solomon asks to be enabled to thank God for His blessing; the procession and gathered animals lead directly into remembrance of niʿma.
terra: The keeper of a gathered company of birds inspects it and notices the missing hoopoe; this directly enacts the section's claim that the lost creature has an owner who knows it is gone.
terra: Solomon demands a clear explanation from the missing hoopoe; the keeper does not treat disappearance as ownerless but requires the absent member to account for its separation.
terra: The absent hoopoe of 27:20 returns after only a short absence and speaks to Solomon; it supplies the found creature's re-entry into the company.

luna: The section's owner searches without knowing a direction; this verse asks who guides people through the darknesses of land and sea, من يهديكم في ظلمات البر والبحر. | terra: God guides people through the darknesses of land and sea and sends winds before mercy; this directly answers the wilderness searcher who does not know which direction to take.
terra: Moses' mother is told to cast him into the river without fear because God will return him to her; separation from the mother begins under an explicit promise of recovery.
terra: Pharaoh's household picks the infant from the water; like the section's found stray, the vulnerable being is taken in by people other than the one who knows he is missing.
terra: Moses' mother tells his sister to follow him, and she watches from a distance unnoticed; the separated one's true family actively tracks rather than forgets him.
terra: After other nursing women are withheld from Moses, his sister directs the finders toward a household that will care for him; the maternal bond becomes the path back to the proper shelter.
terra: God returns Moses to his mother so that her eye may be comforted and she may know the promise is true; this is a complete Quranic recovery of one separated from the maternal side.

luna: The section's image of the lost becoming guided is echoed by Moses, fleeing toward Midian and asking that his Lord guide him to the sound way, سواء السبيل. | terra: As Moses sets toward Midian, he asks his Lord to guide him to the right way; the request supplies the directional uncertainty immediately resolved by finding the held-back flock in 28:23.

luna: The section's lost-herd scene turns on an owner who cannot be found; here Moses finds two women holding their flock back until the shepherds leave, and their father is too old to herd. | terra: Moses finds two women behind the other people, holding their flock back until the shepherds leave; وَوَجَدَ, the rear position, and the detained herd all meet in one scene.

luna: The section's 28:23 scene leaves the women waiting to water their flock; this verse says Moses waters it, then asks his Lord for whatever good He sends, joining animal care to his need. | terra: Moses waters the lagging women's flock and then calls himself poor for whatever good his Lord sends; the scene joins aid reaching those held back with the needy searcher awaiting provision.
terra: One of the women returns to Moses and says her father calls him to repay the watering; the aid given to a delayed flock is answered by provision and entry into a household.

luna: The section's dictionary form هادي names a leader at the head who leads a herd; this verse reverses that role with leaders who call people to the Fire. | terra: Pharaoh and his chiefs are made leaders who call toward the Fire; the foremost figures exercise precisely the opposite office from guides who bring those behind to safety.
terra: Praise belongs to God in the first life and the Hereafter; it is another formulation that places both ends of the section's line under one Lord.
luna: The section says the poor and wandering are not left without provision; this verse points to creatures unable to carry their own provision and says God provides for them and people.
terra: At a single divine call, people emerge from the earth; the call recalls a dispersed creation into responsive presence.

luna: The section's lost camel remains a living creature its owner can seek; this verse uses the section's root ض ل ل for bodies lost into the earth and asks whether they can be created anew, a more final kind of disappearance. | terra: The deniers ask whether, once “lost in the earth,” they can be newly created; the different bodily sense of ضَلَلْنَا extends the lost-animal image to dissolution and return to the Lord.
terra: For believers, gardens are نُزُلًا and جَنَّـٰتُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ; this is the welcoming final shelter contrasted with the fire-shelter of 32:20.
terra: The defiantly disobedient have the Fire as their مَأْوَىٰ and are returned whenever they try to leave; the fold image becomes confinement rather than protective gathering.

luna: The section's dictionary form هادي names a herd's leader; this verse describes leaders who guide by God's command, making animal direction a model for communal guidance. | terra: God appoints leaders who guide by His command when they are patient; leadership and guidance occupy the same forward position described in the section.

terra: When people's fathers are unknown, the community must call them brothers and allies rather than fabricate paternity; this sets a social boundary around the section's claim that human orphanhood is defined from the father's side.
terra: People in the Fire say they obeyed their chiefs and great ones, who led them astray from the way; it is another failed front of the procession, where following produces loss.
terra: Nothing as small as an atom in heaven or earth escapes God's knowledge, and all is in a clear record; it reinforces the boundary against any creature being truly unaccounted for.
terra: Inheritors of the Book divide into one who wrongs himself, one moderate, and one foremost in good; the single community forms a moral sequence with a leading rank.

terra: Sun, moon, night, and day move in an order in which one does not overtake the other and each travels its course; this is a cosmic counterpart to the section's sequence of front and rear positions.
terra: At the trumpet blast, people leave their graves and hasten to their Lord; the Owner's signal summons a dispersed company back toward Him.
terra: One cry suffices for everyone to be brought present before God; it gives the section's returning voice-call an eschatological completion.

luna: The section's flock is an animal community under care; 36:71 says God created livestock that people own, establishing the human-animal relation behind the herd image. | terra: God says He created livestock for people and that they are their owners, لَهَا مَـٰلِكُونَ; the explicit ownership clarifies what is at stake when one animal becomes a ضالّة whose owner is unknown.

luna: The section's herd is cared for as useful livestock; this verse says animals were made manageable, with some for riding and some for food. | terra: The livestock owned in 36:71 are subjected for people, some as mounts and some as food; ownership is expressed as care, use, and accountability for a tamed herd.

luna: The section's dictionary explanation calls camels النعم because of their blessing; this verse names livestock's other benefits and drink and ends by asking for gratitude. | terra: Livestock supply benefits and drinks and call for gratitude; this explains in Quranic terms why the section's herd-name belongs to the semantic family of blessing.
terra: The wrongdoers and their counterparts are ordered gathered; unlike the recovered herd's safe collection, this company is assembled for judgment and then directed toward Hell in 37:23.
terra: The gathered wrongdoers of 37:22 are “guided” to the path of Hell; it is a grim reversal in which guidance and a common destination do not mean rescue.
terra: The birds are gathered, مَحْشُورَةً, and each is returning, أَوَّابٌ; this is a Quranic bird-company gathered back together, closely matching the dictionary scene for تأوّت الطير.

terra: One ewe stands against a flock of ninety-nine ewes whose owner seeks to absorb her into it; the isolated animal, the flock, and a contested claim of ownership make the herd's social boundary visible.
terra: David judges that the owner of many ewes wronged the owner of one by demanding it, then repents; it supplies the moral boundary around the contested incorporation described in 38:23.
terra: Fine standing horses are displayed to Solomon in the evening; they form the equine company whose recall and necks appear in 38:33, matching two secondary details developed in the section.

terra: Between the display and recall of the horses, Solomon calls them a love of “the good” and mentions his Lord; the wording echoes the section's derivation of livestock from the good they contain.

terra: Solomon orders the horses returned and strokes their legs and necks; “return them to me” enacts recalled animals, while ٱلْأَعْنَاقِ matches the section's designation of horses' necks as their foremost parts.

terra: The ayah joins eight livestock pairs with creation in mothers' wombs through layered stages; this gives Quranic form to the section's attention to animal sex and the maternal side of animal orphanhood.
terra: Disbelievers are driven in groups to Hell until its gates open; the group reaches a gated destination, but the fold has become punitive confinement.
terra: Those mindful of their Lord are led in groups to the Garden until its gates open and its keepers greet them; paired with 39:71, this is the safe counterpart of a company brought home.
terra: God makes livestock so that people ride some and eat some; the herd is presented as deliberately provided rather than abandoned in the wilderness.
terra: Livestock carry people toward needs in their hearts, alongside ships; the animal company becomes a means by which a destination can be reached.
terra: God has dispersed living creatures through the heavens and earth and is able to gather them whenever He wills; dispersal and recovered collection are explicitly held by one Owner.

luna: The section calls livestock النعم because they are a blessing; this verse names ships and livestock as mounts, grounding that blessing in the animal's use. | terra: God makes ships and livestock into mounts; the next ayah explicitly tells the rider to remember the Lord's blessing, joining the section's animal, rider, Rabb, and niʿma roots.

luna: The section ends by connecting livestock's name to blessing and the command to speak of God's favor; this verse tells riders to remember their Lord's blessing when mounted and praise the One who subjected the animal. | terra: On settling upon the livestock mounts of 43:12, the rider remembers نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ; this directly reunites the herd-name's “blessing” sense with Rabb and riding.
terra: God knows what the earth diminishes of human bodies and keeps a preserving record; this directly answers the claim of being “lost in the earth” with knowledge that retains every part.
terra: The listener is told to await the day when the caller calls from a near place; the divine summons sets up the rapid emergence and gathering in 50:44.
terra: The earth splits and people hasten out; God calls this an easy gathering, making the response to the caller a universal collection.

luna: The section makes ضالّ a lost animal whose owner seeks it, not a moral charge; this verse explicitly denies that Muhammad has gone astray, ما ضل صاحبكم, distinguishing the senses. | terra: Addressing the same prophetic companion as surah 93, the ayah says he has neither strayed nor erred; it gives the section's ضَالّ a direct later reassurance about the addressee.
terra: The Garden of مأوى stands by the lote tree of the boundary; it carries the section's ordinary animal shelter into the name of an ultimate abode.

luna: The section's first and last positions echo its surah's first-life/Hereafter contrast; this verse says both the Hereafter and the first life belong to God, فلله الآخرة والأولى. | terra: The ayah says that both the latter and the former, ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ, belong to God; the front and rear of the section's line have one Owner.
terra: The Prophet is told to turn away until the caller summons people to a terrible event; it supplies the voice whose gathered, animal-like respondents appear in 54:7.
terra: People emerge from graves like scattered locusts with humbled eyes; the animal comparison makes a dispersed multitude visible just before all hasten toward one caller.
terra: The emerging multitude hastens toward the caller; it completes 54:7's scattered-locust image as a company converging on a voice.
terra: God sends the she-camel as a test and commands watchful patience; the keeper must recognize and protect a particular animal within the community.
terra: Water is divided between the people and the she-camel, with each turn attended; the herd image gains an exact sequence of allotted access rather than a disorderly rush.
terra: The foremost are named twice as the foremost; this isolates the leading position whose closeness and destination are given in the following ayah.
terra: The foremost of 56:10 are brought near to God; the head of the company is defined by proximity to its destination and Owner.
terra: The section's “first” and “last” are positions in one moving line; this ayah joins ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ and ٱلْـَٔاخِرِينَ before the next ayah gathers both groups together.
terra: After 56:49 names the first and last, this ayah says that all are gathered at a known appointment; it gives the whole separated procession one final gathering place.

luna: The section uses first and last for positions in a herd; this verse applies those same dictionary forms to God, الأول والآخر, moving the sequence's terms beyond any created order. | terra: God is named the First and the Last together; the section's two ends of a procession become coincident divine names rather than separated positions.
terra: Believing men and women move with their light running before them toward the announced gardens; a guided forward company is visible immediately before the laggards of 57:13 are separated.
terra: Hypocrites call to the believers to wait so they can take light, but are told to go back and a barrier divides them; the lagging members fail to rejoin the forward company.

luna: The section names the orphan among those vulnerable to delayed provision; this verse includes orphans among the recipients of shared wealth so it does not circulate only among the rich. | terra: Orphans receive a share of public wealth so that it does not circulate only among the rich; the distribution repairs the lag in provision structurally.
luna: The section's lost creature is not ownerless but received into a home; this verse describes the Medinan helpers who made a home for the emigrants and preferred them over themselves.

terra: The person of restricted provision must spend from what God gave, and God promises ease after hardship; constrained means, divine provision, and good arriving after delay closely extend the section's needy figure.
terra: Birds above spread and fold their wings, and none holds them except the Merciful; the flying company remains upheld by its divine keeper rather than being abandoned.

terra: A person's close clan is described as the family that shelters him, تُـْٔوِيهِ; the ayah preserves the social sense of being gathered into a protecting group even as judgment dissolves that loyalty.
terra: The warning addresses whoever chooses to advance or fall behind, يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ; the herd's opposed positions become a moral choice made within a single human company.

luna: The section's first, last, advancing, and lagging members give spatial force to its root ء خ ر; this verse speaks of what a person sent ahead and left behind, بما قدم وأخر, transferring sequence to deeds. | terra: A person is told what he sent ahead and left behind, قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ; the section's spatial front and rear shift into the temporal ordering of one's deeds.
terra: People love the immediate life; this preference occupies the “first” end of the section's pair and is set against neglect of the Hereafter in 75:21.
terra: People leave the Hereafter aside; with 75:20 it shows a procession morally disordered by attachment to what comes first.

luna: The section joins orphanhood with need; this verse describes feeding the needy, orphan, and captive despite loving the food oneself. | terra: The righteous feed an orphan, alongside the needy and captive, despite valuing the food; this is beneficence actually reaching the figure whose name the section derives from delayed good.

luna: The section's herd goes out to graze; this verse says God brings water and pasture out of the earth, أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها, the setting that feeds it. | terra: God brings out water and pasture from the earth; the next two ayat explicitly assign that pasture as provision to people and livestock.

luna: The section treats livestock as a blessing; after 79:31's water and pasture, this verse names that provision as enjoyment for people and their cattle, متاعا لكم ولأنعامكم. | terra: The earth's water and pasture are provision for people and their livestock; the grazing scene is set within the Provider's preparation of the land.
terra: For the one who prefers the nearer life, Hell is the مَأْوَىٰ; the familiar word for shelter is turned into the destination of a disordered preference.
terra: For the one who fears the Lord and restrains desire, the Garden is the مَأْوَىٰ; paired with 79:39, it distinguishes the two ultimate gathering places.

luna: The section's herd depends on pasture; this verse names fruit and herbage, and 80:32 completes the scene by assigning them to people and their livestock. | terra: The earth produces fruit and pasture; 80:32 identifies it as provision for people and livestock, giving the herd a prepared feeding ground.

luna: The section calls the camel herd a blessing; after 80:31's produce and herbage, this verse says the provision is for people and their livestock, ولأنعامكم. | terra: The food and pasture are a provision for people and livestock; the animal line lives by a provision that precedes and awaits it.
luna: The section's lost camel has an owner who searches and restores it to shelter; at the Hour, prized camels are left unattended, العشار عطلت, a direct reversal of care.
terra: Wild beasts are gathered together; this is the Quran's compressed counterpart to the section's wild-animal leaders and the final collection of scattered animals.
terra: Every soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind; this repeated secondary sense shows that the line's ordering can also describe consequences placed before or deferred.
terra: God measures and then guides; the concise sequence presents direction as part of the ordering allotted to creatures rather than recovery by chance.
luna: The section begins with a herd going out to graze; this verse names the pasture God brings forth, المرعى, using the same pasture root as the section's grazing dictionary forms.
luna: The section's herd depends on pasture; this next verse shows that pasture drying into dark stubble, adding the passing cycle of the ground on which it feeds.

luna: The section's first and last herd members become the first life and Hereafter in 93:4; this verse says people prefer the nearer life, بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا, naming the choice that 93:4 corrects. | terra: People prefer the nearer life; beside the section's front/back reading of first and latter, this ayah makes preference for the first side of the pair the error explained in 87:17.

luna: The section's dictionary terms for first and last extend into 93:4's Hereafter and first life; this verse says the Hereafter is better and more lasting, والآخرة خير وأبقى. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting, while 87:16 says people prefer the nearer life; the pair gives the first/last ordering a duration and value beyond spatial sequence.
luna: The section connects God's finding and enriching the needy to care for the orphan; this verse says people read expanded provision as honor, a belief the following orphan rebuke corrects.
luna: The section joins need with later provision; this verse says people read restricted provision as humiliation, and 89:17 answers that the orphan is the one they fail to honor.

luna: The section's orphan is not to be oppressed; this verse directly rebukes failure to honor the orphan, and 89:18 adds neglect of feeding the poor. | terra: The rebuke “you do not honor the orphan” names the neglect that makes good late, directly opposing the shelter and care narrated and commanded in surah 93.
luna: The section's orphan is part of the vulnerable flock of people needing care; this verse names the failure to urge feeding the poor, completing 89:17's orphan rebuke.
luna: The section connects care with what reaches the vulnerable; this verse names feeding on a day of hunger, and 90:15 specifies the near orphan as a recipient.

luna: The section's orphan receives kindness after a vulnerable beginning; this verse specifies feeding an orphan who is a relative, يتيما ذا مقربة, as a difficult good deed. | terra: Feeding an orphaned relative on a day of hunger gives the section's slow-arriving good a concrete form and ties the exposed child back to kin.
luna: The section joins the orphan's delayed kindness with the poor person's need; this verse names a destitute person in misery, continuing 90:15's account of whom care reaches.
terra: The messenger identifies the animal as “God's she-camel” and protects her allotted drink; female camel, named Owner, and ordered access to water meet in one warning.

luna: The section's source root ء خ ر moves from the rear of a herd to the Hereafter; this verse pairs the Hereafter and first life as belonging to God, للآخرة والأولى. | terra: God declares that both the Hereafter and the first life belong to Him; the two endpoints that the section pictures as herd positions are held within one ownership.
terra: The same prophetic addressee is promised that ease accompanies hardship; this gives the section's delayed beneficence a closely related reassurance.
terra: The promise of ease with hardship is repeated for emphasis; repetition makes eventual relief dependable for the addressee who was found exposed and needy.
terra: The opening oath depicts running horses breathing hard; it activates the section's equine leading and movement details, though here the animals charge rather than graze.
terra: The horses raid at dawn; their forceful morning advance is a martial reversal of the section's herd quietly beginning to pasture early in the day.
terra: The people are commanded to worship the Lord of “this House”; Rabb is identified through a fixed home, preparing the feeding and security named in 106:4.
terra: The Lord of the House feeds against hunger and secures against fear; Owner, dwelling, provision, and safety combine as the human counterpart of a tended fold.

luna: The section commands that the orphan not be oppressed; this verse identifies repelling the orphan as a mark of denial, a direct reversal of shelter and care. | terra: The denier violently repels the orphan; that expulsion from protection is the exact reversal of calling the vulnerable one back and giving shelter.
luna: The section's orphan-care image includes provision for vulnerable people; following 107:2, this verse condemns failure to urge feeding the poor.
